{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793109140712,"sessionID":"ses_e825ebb36ffe02V6IiGRZ2p7n5","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01WKqz2QvTeQ9YgGo8SkmtAo","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/nbody_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r5/nbody/nbody.cpp","content":"#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nconstexpr double SOFTENING = 1e-9;\nconstexpr double DT = 0.01;\n\n// Threads per block for both kernels. Also the shared-memory tile size used by\n// the force kernel.\nconstexpr int BLOCK_SIZE = 256;\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                              \\\n    do {                                                                              \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                    \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                    \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,          \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                        \\\n            exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                       \\\n        }                                                                             \\\n    } while (0)\n\nstruct Vec3 {\n    double x, y, z;\n    constexpr Vec3(const double x = 0, const double y = 0, const double z = 0) noexcept : x(x), y(y), z(z) {}\n};\n\nstruct Body {\n    Vec3 pos;\n    Vec3 vel;\n};\n\nvoid randomizeBodies(std::vector<Body>& bodies, unsigned int seed = 42) {\n    for (auto& body : bodies) {\n        body.pos.x = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.pos.y = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.pos.z = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.vel.x = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.vel.y = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.vel.z = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n    }\n}\n\n// One thread per body. Positions of all bodies are staged through shared memory\n// in tiles of BLOCK_SIZE. Tiles are visited in increasing j order and each thread\n// accumulates its force sequentially over j = 0..n-1, which matches the\n// summation order of the original serial algorithm.\n__global__ void computeForcesKernel(Body* __restrict__ bodies, const int n) {\n    __shared__ double sx[BLOCK_SIZE];\n    __shared__ double sy[BLOCK_SIZE];\n    __shared__ double sz[BLOCK_SIZE];\n\n    const int t = threadIdx.x;\n    const int i = blockIdx.x * BLOCK_SIZE + t;\n    const bool active = i < n;\n\n    double px = 0.0, py = 0.0, pz = 0.0;\n    if (active) {\n        px = bodies[i].pos.x;\n        py = bodies[i].pos.y;\n        pz = bodies[i].pos.z;\n    }\n\n    double Fx = 0.0, Fy = 0.0, Fz = 0.0;\n\n    for (int base = 0; base < n; base += BLOCK_SIZE) {\n        const int j = base + t;\n        if (j < n) {\n            sx[t] = bodies[j].pos.x;\n            sy[t] = bodies[j].pos.y;\n            sz[t] = bodies[j].pos.z;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        const int count = min(BLOCK_SIZE, n - base);\n        if (active) {\n            for (int k = 0; k < count; ++k) {\n                const double dx = sx[k] - px;\n                const double dy = sy[k] - py;\n                const double dz = sz[k] - pz;\n                const double distSqr = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz + SOFTENING;\n                const double invDist = 1.0 / sqrt(distSqr);\n                const double invDist3 = invDist * invDist * invDist;\n\n                Fx += dx * invDist3;\n                Fy += dy * invDist3;\n                Fz += dz * invDist3;\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    if (active) {\n        bodies[i].vel.x += DT * Fx;\n        bodies[i].vel.y += DT * Fy;\n        bodies[i].vel.z += DT * Fz;\n    }\n}\n\n__global__ void integrateBodiesKernel(Body* __restrict__ bodies, const int n) {\n    const int i = blockIdx.x * BLOCK_SIZE + threadIdx.x;\n    if (i < n) {\n        bodies[i].pos.x += bodies[i].vel.x * DT;\n        bodies[i].pos.y += bodies[i].vel.y * DT;\n        bodies[i].pos.z += bodies[i].vel.z * DT;\n    }\n}\n\n// Device-side wrappers. d_bodies must point to n bodies in device memory.\nvoid computeForces(Body* d_bodies, const int n) {\n    const int grid = (n + BLOCK_SIZE - 1) / BLOCK_SIZE;\n    computeForcesKernel<<<grid, BLOCK_SIZE>>>(d_bodies, n);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n}\n\nvoid integrateBodies(Body* d_bodies, const int n) {\n    const int grid = (n + BLOCK_SIZE - 1) / BLOCK_SIZE;\n    integrateBodiesKernel<<<grid, BLOCK_SIZE>>>(d_bodies, n);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n}\n\ndouble computeTotalEnergy(const std::vector<Body>& bodies) {\n    double energy = 0.0;\n    const size_t n = bodies.size();\n    \n    // Kinetic energy (assuming unit mass)\n    for (const auto& body : bodies) {\n        energy += 0.5 * (body.vel.x * body.vel.x + \n                        body.vel.y * body.vel.y + \n                        body.vel.z * body.vel.z);\n    }\n    \n    // Potential energy (assuming unit mass for all bodies)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            const double dx = bodies[j].pos.x - bodies[i].pos.x;\n            const double dy = bodies[j].pos.y - bodies[i].pos.y;\n            const double dz = bodies[j].pos.z - bodies[i].pos.z;\n            const double dist = std::sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz + SOFTENING);\n            energy -= 1.0 / dist;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return energy;\n}\n\n// Validate that simulation produces finite, reasonable values\nbool validateSimulation(const std::vector<Body>& bodies) {\n    for (const auto& body : bodies) {\n        // Check for NaN or Inf values\n        if (!std::isfinite(body.pos.x) || !std::isfinite(body.pos.y) || !std::isfinite(body.pos.z) ||\n            !std::isfinite(body.vel.x) || !std::isfinite(body.vel.y) || !std::isfinite(body.vel.z)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: found NaN or Inf value in body state\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n        \n        // Check for extreme values (bodies shouldn't fly off to infinity)\n        const double maxPos = 1e6;\n        const double maxVel = 1e6;\n        if (std::abs(body.pos.x) > maxPos || std::abs(body.pos.y) > maxPos || std::abs(body.pos.z) > maxPos) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: body position exceeds reasonable bounds\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n        if (std::abs(body.vel.x) > maxVel || std::abs(body.vel.y) > maxVel || std::abs(body.vel.z) > maxVel) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: body velocity exceeds reasonable bounds\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of bodies (default: 1024)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -s <num>     Number of simulation steps (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation (checks energy conservation)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    int numBodies = 1024;\n    int numSteps = 10;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numBodies = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-s\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numSteps = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"N-Body Simulation\\n\");\n    printf(\"Number of bodies: %d\\n\", numBodies);\n    printf(\"Number of steps: %d\\n\", numSteps);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Initialize bodies\n    std::vector<Body> bodies(numBodies);\n    randomizeBodies(bodies);\n\n    // Allocate device memory and upload the initial state once. The state stays\n    // on the device for the whole simulation.\n    const int n = static_cast<int>(bodies.size());\n    Body* d_bodies = nullptr;\n    if (n > 0) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_bodies, bodies.size() * sizeof(Body)));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(d_bodies, bodies.data(), bodies.size() * sizeof(Body), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    }\n    \n    // Run simulation\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    \n    if (n > 0) {\n        for (int step = 0; step < numSteps; ++step) {\n            computeForces(d_bodies, n);\n            integrateBodies(d_bodies, n);\n        }\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaDeviceSynchronize());\n    }\n    \n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    // Retrieve final state for reporting and validation.\n    if (n > 0) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(bodies.data(), d_bodies, bodies.size() * sizeof(Body), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(d_bodies));\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Simulation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n    \n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        // Serialize body positions and velocities for hashing\n        std::vector<double> bodyData;\n        bodyData.reserve(numBodies * 6);\n        for (const auto& body : bodies) {\n            bodyData.push_back(body.pos.x);\n            bodyData.push_back(body.pos.y);\n            bodyData.push_back(body.pos.z);\n            bodyData.push_back(body.vel.x);\n            bodyData.push_back(body.vel.y);\n            bodyData.push_back(body.vel.z);\n        }\n        print_results(bodyData, \"Bodies\");\n    }\n    \n    // Validation: check that simulation produces finite, reasonable values\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating simulation results...\\n\");\n        \n        if (validateSimulation(bodies)) {\n            // Report final energy for reference\n            double finalEnergy = computeTotalEnergy(bodies);\n            printf(\"Final energy: %.6f\\n\", finalEnergy);\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return 0;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file I changed only `nbody/nbody.cpp` and `nbody/CMakeLists.txt`.\n\n**What changed**\n- **Kernels:** One thread per body. Positions are staged through shared memory in tiles of 256. Each thread sums over j in the same 0..N-1 order as the original, so the only numerical difference is FMA contraction (below).\n- **Data movement:** Bodies are uploaded once, all steps run on the device, and the state is copied back once for `-r` and `-v`. The timed region covers the kernel work only, matching what the original timed.\n- **Build:** The `.cpp` is compiled as CUDA via the `LANGUAGE CUDA` source property, so no new files were needed. `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` defaults to `native`, and the minimum CMake version is now 3.24 for that.\n\n**Results (RTX 3090, scratch build)**\n- N=4096, 10 steps: 1239 ms on CPU → about 86 ms on GPU.\n- N=16384, 10 steps: about 313 ms on GPU.\n- `-v` validation passes; N=0 and N=1 work.\n- Build has no warnings.\n\n**Numerical note**\nWith nvcc's default FMA contraction, the `-r` hash for N=1024 is `89e47fc72fac2624`, while the original CPU build gives `1eed6713692b7ce8`. The values agree to about 1e-12 relative. The gap comes from FMA contraction, not the algorithm: when FMA is disabled on both sides, the CPU and GPU hashes match exactly (`37bf5bbdacd6cae0`). I kept the default for speed, since `--fmad=false` cost about 25% at N=16384. If you need bit-exact agreement with the original build, add `--fmad=false` to the CUDA flags in CMakeLists.txt.\n\nThe `output.txt` in the workspace is a leftover session log, so I left it alone.","time":{"start":1793109238606,"end":1793109240482}}}
